t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary of the Treasury (or the Secretary’s delegate) shall make available a form (or modify existing forms) for use by individuals to direct that a portion of any refund of overpayment of tax imposed by chapter 1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 be paid directly to an individual retirement plan (as defined in section 7701(a)(37) of such Code) of such individual. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The form required by subsection (a) shall be made available for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2006.

fable.w: The section only directs the Treasury to provide a tax form that lets individuals route their own refunds into an individual retirement plan. The tempting reading is that individuals "directing" a refund is outside involvement, but that is a personal transaction about their own money, not consultation on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: shall make available a form (or modify existing forms) for use by individuals to direct that a portion of any refund of overpayment of tax

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary to provide a form for individuals to use when claiming a tax refund. This is an administrative procedure for individuals to access a benefit (a tax refund) or manage their own finances. It does not involve the government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The interaction is one-way (government provides form, individual uses it) and does not constitute participation in a federal decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of the Treasury (or the Secretary’s delegate) shall make available a form (or modify existing forms) for use by individuals to direct that a portion of any refund of overpayment of tax imposed by chapter 1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 be paid directly to an individual retirement plan

opus.w: The tempting reading is that individuals outside the government are taking part because they fill out a form that tells Treasury what to do with their refund. That fails the definition. The form only lets a taxpayer choose where their own refund goes, which is like applying for or electing a benefit, not giving input before a federal policy decision. The section also requires no rulemaking, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with outside parties.
opus.s: The Secretary of the Treasury (or the Secretary’s delegate) shall make available a form (or modify existing forms) for use by individuals to direct that a portion of any refund of overpayment of tax imposed by chapter 1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 be paid directly to an individual retirement plan

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the creation of a form for individuals to direct their tax refunds to an IRA. This is a transactional mechanism for individuals to manage their own funds, not a process of consultation or coordination with the government before a federal decision is made. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this scenario is analogous to an individual directing payment rather than participating in a policy decision.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Treasury (or the Secretary’s delegate) shall make available a form (or modify existing forms) for use by individuals to direct that a portion of any refund of overpayment of tax imposed by chapter 1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 be paid directly to an individual retirement plan
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allowing individuals to direct their tax refunds to an IRA is a form of "participation" because it involves the public interacting with the government's tax system. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and focuses on consultation or coordination *before* a federal decision is made. Here, the individual is simply exercising a right to allocate their own money (a refund they are already owed) to a specific account. There is no federal decision being made that requires input from the public; the government is merely providing a mechanism for payment. The interaction is transactional, not deliberative or advisory.
